Office Visit - Follow-up
Patient: Greta Delacroix | DOB: 12/10/1951 | MRN: SYN-4920281
Date of service: 08/05/2025 | Dr. Teodor Ellery, MD

History of present illness:
73-year-old woman seen for follow-up of low back pain. Low back pain radiating to the right leg for 12 weeks.

Treatment to date:
Two months of supervised exercise sessions plus over-the-counter anti-inflammatories have not brought lasting relief.

History:
Past medical history: hyperlipidemia, hypertension.
Medications: atorvastatin 20 mg nightly; lisinopril 10 mg daily.

Review of systems:
No trouble controlling urine or stool, no numbness in the groin area, no fevers, stable weight, and no prior malignancy.

Physical exam:
Back: tenderness over the lower lumbar paraspinal muscles; straight-leg raise positive on the right at 50 degrees.
She cannot rise onto her toes on the right as well as on the other side, the ankle jerk is reduced on the right, and touch feels dull along the outer edge of that foot.

Assessment and plan:
Assessment: right S1 lumbar radiculopathy.
Plan: MRI lumbar spine without contrast to evaluate for disc herniation; home exercise program; follow up after imaging.
